name: VisualTimer
shortDescription: A countdown or a stopwatch shown on screen. It can count the time itself or show a scene timer.
description: A timer shown on screen, with an icon and a background:
- a **countdown**, to give a time limit (with a warning style at the end, and a condition when it is finished),
- a **stopwatch**, to show the time spent in a level or a race.
It counts the time itself, with actions to start, pause, restart it or add time (like a bonus).
It can also show a **scene timer**: write its name in the "Scene timer to show" property. To show an object timer, change its elapsed time every frame.
Ready-to-use timers in many styles are in the asset store [timers pack](https://editor.gdevelop.io/?initial-dialog=asset-store&asset-pack=timers-visual-timers).

propertyDescriptors.label: Mode
propertyDescriptors.name: Mode
propertyDescriptors.description: A countdown shows the time left, a stopwatch shows the elapsed time.

propertyDescriptors.label: Countdown duration
propertyDescriptors.name: Duration
propertyDescriptors.description: The time to count down from.

propertyDescriptors.label: Start when created
propertyDescriptors.name: ShouldStartOnCreation
propertyDescriptors.description: Start counting as soon as the timer is created.

propertyDescriptors.label: Warning when the time left is under
propertyDescriptors.name: WarningDuration
propertyDescriptors.description: The countdown is shown in its warning style (red and blinking) at the end. 0 to never show it.

propertyDescriptors.label: Scene timer to show
propertyDescriptors.name: SceneTimerName
propertyDescriptors.description: Leave it empty to let the object count the time. Or write the name of a scene timer (used with the "Start (or reset) a scene timer" action) to show it.

events.comment: "Has just finished" is true during the frame after the countdown reached 0, so that it can be checked in the events of the scene.
The time shown: the time left of a countdown, or the elapsed time of a stopwatch.
A countdown rounds up (it shows 0:01 until the very end), a stopwatch rounds down.

parameters: ToString(floor(ShownSeconds / 3600)) + ":" + StrRepeat("0", 2 - StrLength(ToString(mod(floor(ShownSeconds / 60), 60)))) + ToString(mod(floor(ShownSeconds / 60), 60)) + ":" + StrRepeat("0", 2 - StrLength(ToString(mod(ShownSeconds, 60)))) + ToString(mod(ShownSeconds, 60))

events.comment: At the end of a countdown, the warning style is shown, blinking twice a second.

eventsFunctions.name: Start
eventsFunctions.description: Start the timer, or start it again after it was paused.

eventsFunctions.name: Restart
eventsFunctions.description: Set the timer back to its beginning (the full duration of a countdown, or 0 for a stopwatch) and start it.

eventsFunctions.name: AddTime

events.comment: A countdown gets more time left (even after it finished: the time left starts from 0), a stopwatch more elapsed time.
More time left than the duration: the duration grows.

eventsFunctions.description: Add time to the timer: more time left for a countdown (use a negative value to remove time), more elapsed time for a stopwatch.

eventsFunctions.name: IsRunning
eventsFunctions.description: Check if the timer is running (started and not paused).

eventsFunctions.name: HasJustFinished
eventsFunctions.sentence: The countdown of _PARAM0_ has just finished
eventsFunctions.description: Check if the countdown has just reached 0. It is true during one frame only, so it can be used without "Trigger once".

eventsFunctions.name: TimeLeft
eventsFunctions.description: the time left of the countdown, in seconds.

eventsFunctions.name: ElapsedTime
eventsFunctions.description: the elapsed time, in seconds. Change it every frame to show the timer of an object, like Player.ObjectTimerElapsedTime("Dash").

eventsFunctions.name: CountdownDuration
eventsFunctions.description: the duration of the countdown, in seconds.
